methodology: Both the original research topic and the generated technical specification were decomposed into atomic units by identifying individual requirements, features, behaviors, and constraints. Each atomic unit was designed to be independent, self-contained, technically specific, unambiguous, and implementable as a single requirement. This involved breaking down complex sentences into their core components and ensuring each component represented a distinct and verifiable aspect of the counter's functionality.
mindtraced_atomic_units: Counter has a synchronous active-high reset input.
Reset input resets the counter to 0 on the next clock edge.
Counter has an enable input named 'slowena'.
Counter increments its value on each clock edge only when 'slowena' is asserted (high).
Counter maintains its current value when 'slowena' is deasserted (low).
Counter's output 'q' is a 4-bit register representing the current count value.
spec_atomic_units: Module top_module has clk, slowena, reset inputs and q output.
Combinational logic determines the next state of the counter.
When reset is high, output q is forced to 0 (synchronous reset).
When slowena is high and reset is low, the counter increments.
If slowena is low, the counter holds its current value.
Counter increments from 0 to 9.
When the counter reaches 9, the next increment resets the counter to 0.
Reset Logic Block forces output q to 0 when reset is high.
Enable Logic Block controls incrementing based on slowena input.
Incrementer Block increments the current value of the counter (q) by 1.
Wrap-Around Logic Block detects when the counter reaches the value 9.
Output Multiplexer selects the final value of q based on reset, enable, and wrap-around conditions.
Output q changes only on the rising edge of clk.
If reset is high at the rising edge of clk, q is set to 0.
If reset is low and slowena is high at the rising edge of clk, q increments, wrapping around to 0 after reaching 9.
Counter uses a 4-bit register q.
State transitions occur on the rising edge of the clock.
Non-blocking assignments are used to update the value of q.
Reset is synchronous.
Enable signal slowena controls whether the counter increments or holds its current value on each clock cycle.
